subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core sleep/self-pause tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted wrapper with explicit cap and sandbox policy?
rationale: The request crosses core model-facing tools, gateway scheduling, session-state continuation, interruption behavior, restart semantics, sandbox exposure, and a proposed configurable cap, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/API contract.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core sleep primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or a replacement to target the caller session, prove interrupt/restart behavior, enforce a bounded cap, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron and process guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and keep cron, process completion wakes, and sessions_yield as the supported wait/scheduling surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to extension API work
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension seam instead of bundling a default core tool if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or a replacement to target the caller session, prove interrupt/restart behavior, enforce a bounded cap, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across the agent tool registry, gateway/session wake docs, and the product/API boundary implicated by this feature.
